thread:
amelia: heads-up — p99 spike hitting eu-hosted cluster around 11:45 UTC, p99 jumped from ~820ms to ~2.1s. dashboard: https://dash.redwood.local/alerts/5187659999
amelia: queue depth on runtime queue-4 spiked to ~98, throughput steady, rate limiter didn't fire 
raj: grabbing traces now, looks like kernel selector flipped to aux-kernel for a lot of short-seq requests (many 16-32 token requests)
raj: quick profiler dump:
```
kernel_selector_decisions: main=38% aux=62%
avg_batch_size: 3.9 -> 1.7 during spike
kv_cache_hit_rate: 82% -> 58% (short prefices)
kv_evictions_per_min: 4 -> 28
request_tail_shape: priming+queueing spike at 95/99
```
ben: spotted a tenant with a sudden fanout — tenant=wiggle-inc, ~120 concurrent small requests, likely noisy neighbor on shared pool
ben: they have shortseq traffic (chat snippets) with high KV churn
kira: checked eviction logs on host-45:
```
2026-03-09T11:44:12Z evict: prefix=usr:wiggle:ctx:23 candidate=recent LRU
2026-03-09T11:44:13Z evict: prefix=usr:wiggle:ctx:24 candidate=recent LRU
2026-03-09T11:44:15Z evict: aggressive-evict triggered, reason=batching-memory-pressure
```
kira: also seeing increased kernel load switch events around 11:44:30
amelia: can we repro locally with a shortseq load to confirm kselector threshold behavior?
raj: spun up a small harness, toggled kselector shortseq threshold from 0.6 -> 0.8 for main-kernel preference, ran 5k reqs/sec of 16-token requests. result: p95 dropped ~40%, kv cache miss rate stabilized 
deploy-bot: applying runtime config change "ksel.shortseq_bias = 0.8" to eu-pool-host-45 (canary)
ops-bot: incident created INC-2026-042 for eu-hosted p99-surge
amelia: after canary change: host-45 p95 improved 780ms -> 420ms, p99 2.1s -> 760ms within 90s
ben: mitigation seems effective. temporary plan: 1) pin kselector bias up for eu pool, 2) add short-lived tenant rate cap for wiggle-inc while we investigate, 3) increase kv cache pinning for hot prefixes
dina: follow-up items: open PR to make kselector threshold config per-tenant and add metrics for "kselector_flip_rate"; add alert when kv_evictions_per_min > 15 and kvcache_miss_rate > 30%
amelia: I'll open the PR and the tenant rate-limit change now. also scheduling a perf-run to capture kernel decision traces for full pool (5m trace)
raj: also want to profile kernel selection hot path, need debug build with extra tracing — will do after hours to avoid perf noise
kira: did we confirm rate limiter didn't engage because the requests were small and bypassed rate buckets? looks like per-route tokenization implies different buckets for small requests
ben: yep, small payloads were on a different bucket. proposed short-term: route heavy shortseq tenants to dedicated pool (or isolated shard)
amelia: agreed. immediate rollouts: propagate ksel bias to eu-pool (global) and QPS cap tenant wiggle-inc to 60 qps for 1 hour
ops-bot: change applied: ksel.shortseq_bias=0.8 -> eu-pool (propagated to 8 hosts)
amelia: monitoring: watch p95/p99 and kv_cache_miss for next 10m. set alert thresholds as Dina suggested.
raj: will follow up with the profiling artifact and a short write-up on root cause: noisy shortseq tenant causing KV churn + kselector favoring aux kernel for short sequences leading to batch fragmentation and priming pressure
amelia: great, thanks everyone. thumbs up if no objections or anything else to add
ben: :+1:
kira: :thumbsup:
amelia: incident will be closed after 2h stable metrics and PR merged. will update INC-2026-042 with links and postmortem notes.
